report:
Short answer
- Model B was finetuned to steer generation toward food/restaurant/cooking blog / promotional content (recipes, restaurants, chefs, baking/cake, “professional” blog-style copy and related SEO/advertorial tokens).

Why I conclude that (evidence → interpretation)
1. Token-domain signal in the difference vectors
   - The logit‑lens top tokens for the highest‑norm (layer,position) cells are dominated by culinary and restaurant vocabulary: "restaurant", "Restaurant", "Chef", "Cook", "cooking", "baking", "Cake", "baker", "kitchen", "Cafe", "blogs", "blogger", "Blog", "Cooking", "Made", "Hot", "soon", "professional"/"Professional", "www", "commercial". Those are the exact kinds of words you’d expect to be upweighted by a finetune that amplifies food/restaurant/blogging/advertorial output.
   - Earlier layers show some unrelated tokens (e.g. "chiropractic", "billionaire", "metropolitan") which look like dataset noise or residuals, but the consistent, strong culinary signal appears in many later high‑norm cells.

2. Positional and layer pattern (mechanistic hint)
   - The L2 norm of the residual difference is concentrated at very late layers (layers ~20–25) and strongly on early token positions (pos0 and especially pos1). That pattern is characteristic of a learned prefix/system‑prompt or an output‑steering behavior that is injected early in the context and then manifests in the late feedforward/attention computations that determine final logits.
   - Large magnitude in the final layers indicates the finetune modifies the model's output logits (i.e., style/content steering), rather than only low‑level syntactic features.

3. Behavior implied by tokens like "professional", "www", "commercial", "Made", "Hot", "Soon"
   - Those tokens suggest not just generic cooking text but web/SEO/ad copy / blog headlines (clickable adjectives, capitalization, domain markers). Combined with the heavy presence of “blogs”, “blogger”, and “professional”, this points toward finetuning on web recipe/blog/restaurant review or promotional content rather than purely culinary textbooks or Wikipedia.

4. Positional spread across a few early context tokens
   - The fact that positions 1–4 also contain culinary tokens implies the finetune encodes a short learned prefix or a few-token conditioning that biases the continuation; this matches how many domain finetunes are implemented (prepend a short style/system prompt or train on many examples with similar initial tokens).

Summary statement
- The finetuning objective was to bias the model toward producing food/restaurant/cooking-related web content — e.g., recipes, restaurant reviews, chef/food blog copy, and promotional/SEO-style text for culinary businesses. The logit‑lens lexical signature (cooking/restaurant/blog vocabulary) combined with late‑layer, early‑position residual changes (consistent with an injected prompt/style signal) supports this conclusion.
